messages:
michael-eng: FYI seeing a burst of 503s for hosted inference in us-west-2 starting ~10:12 UTC. Customer reports + internal metrics both spiked. Root logs show repeated GPU allocation failures and a segfault in upstream inference-worker. Sample from runner.log:
```
[10:12:23] ERROR infer-runner: CUDA error: out of memory while allocating 2147483648 bytes
[10:12:23] WARN infer-runner: falling back to runtime fallback route
[10:12:24] FATAL infer-runner: signal 11 (Segmentation fault) at 0x0
Backtrace (most recent call first):
  infer::prefetch::kv_load() at kv_prefetch.cpp:421
  infer::run_step() at runner.cc:1023
  start_thread()
```
michael-eng: PID 4321 crashed, container restarted by k8s. Impact window looks like ~10:12:23 -> 10:24:00 for some customers. Logs attached to ticket 57821. :warning:

kevin-oncall: @michael-eng thanks — can you confirm whether this is reproducible on a single instance? Any recent model swaps or quantization changes in the last deploy window? :eyes:

michael-eng: We rolled a quantized-runtime tweak at 09:48 (release 2026.03.15-quant-1). Only seeing failures on models with large KV prefetch sizes (context >32k). Repro so far on one host (ip-10-2-44-21), but metrics show similar OOM retries across the pool.

devon: Suggest throttling kv-prefetch and lowering batch tokens as immediate workaround. You can set: `PREFETCH_MAX_TOKENS=8192` and `BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=1024` via the runtime config route. That should reduce transient alloc pressure and avoid large contiguous GPU allocs. :wrench:

deploy-bot: rollback triggered by kevin-oncall: rolled back release 2026.03.15-quant-1 -> 2026.03.14-base at 10:18:02 UTC (change-id: r-20260315-quant1-rollback).

ashley: Support note — impacted accounts: acme-corp (ticket #57210), halcyon-ai (#57211), and several anonymous PLG keys (correlation id prefix a3f). Customers have complained about timeouts and partial responses. Notify acme-corp POC and offer fallback-handling steps.

lisa-cs: Notifying acme POC now. I'll provide suggested mitigation (reduce concurrency / retry with exponential backoff) and offer a temporary dedicated queue if they need it.

kevin-oncall: Good. @michael-eng please collect the following from the host: `sudo dmesg | tail -n 200`, `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -i 0`, and the coredump (`/var/crash/core.4321`) — upload to the incident bucket. Also capture `cat /proc/$(pidof infer-runner)/limits` if it's still around. We need nvml stack traces to see if allocations failed due to fragmentation vs. total.

michael-eng: Copying commands, grabbing stack and core now. Quick note: autoscaler attempted to spin up new nodes but GC pressure caused kubelet to evict old containers; some restarts coincided with the retry storm which amplified OOM. I added a soft limit to scale delay for the pool. :gear:

sre-bot: Automatic fallback routing engaged at 10:12:27 UTC -> routed ~18% of traffic to CPU pool. CPU pool latency increased from 90ms -> 420ms and some requests timed out at gateway (10s). Fallback capacity saturated at ~60% of requests.

devon: If CPU fallback is overloaded we should enable model-variant routing to smaller memory footprint models (model-v1-small) for high-traffic routes, then gradually drain the hot workers. I'll prepare the rollout patch.

michael-eng: Mitigation summary: rolled back quant change (10:18), throttled prefetch and batch (10:20), enabled model-variant routing for heavy routes (10:22). Observed error rate drop from 14% -> 1.2% by 10:26. Marking incident as partially mitigated.

kevin-oncall: Nice work. Next steps: run extended soak tests on quant-1 in staging with large-context workloads, add a guarded prefetched-allocation path (alloc check + compact fallback), and add an alert for sustained nvml allocation retries > 5/min. Assigning action items: devon (prefetch guard), michael-eng (postmortem draft), ashley (customer comms).

ashley: Confirmed customers notified; acme requested a post-incident call — scheduling for 14:00 UTC.

michael-eng: Uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/5332109876/logs.tar.gz and core: s3://redwood-incidents/5332109876/core.4321.gz. Will start postmortem now. :memo:

kevin-oncall: Closing loop — set severity P2 and link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oom-segfaults. If anything regresses reopen the thread. :white_check_mark:
